newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, March 20.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, March 20.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - Britain's FTSE 100 index suffered its biggest one-day fall in points of the year so far as Wall Street dropped on renewed fears of an imminent rise in U.S. interest rates. The FTSE 100 index closed 74.1 points lower at 4,258.1, its biggest loss since an 88-point tumble last December.

FRANKFURT - German equities ended bourse trade sharply lower, with the dollar also lower but stable, providing support. The narrowing of losses overnight on Wall Street also underpinned trade. But fears of a more serious correction later this week or early next week gave the market jitters, while the triple-witching on Friday muted sentiment. The DAX-30 index ended at 3,264.67 down 51.26 points. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,247.03.

PARIS - French shares closed sharply lower after being swamped by losses in the late afternoon, although the CAC index did partially recoup the declines, comments by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan fuelled fears of a preemptive rise in interest rates at next Tuesday's Fed policy meeting. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 43.05 points or 1.66 percent at 2,553.72.

ZURICH - Swiss shares slumped two percent as U.S. economic data, the weaker opening on Wall Street, the sagging dollar and remarks by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan put pressure on stocks. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) slipped 50.84 points or 1.77 percent to 2,828.66.
TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market is closed for a National Holiday, trading will resume on Friday.
On Wednesday, the 225-share Nikkei average finished at 18,493.71, up 48.51 points or 0.26 percent.

HONG KONG - Concerns about higher interest rates continued to pummel Hong Kong stocks with the Hang Seng Index closing with heavy losses as investors awaited next Tuesday's U.S. Federal Reserve meeting. The Hang Seng index slid 179.09 points or 1.42 percent to close at 12,472.33.

SYDNEY - Australian stocks shook off a weaker Dow, closing up slightly as firmer commodity prices helped a stronger resources sector, many investors remained on the sidelines in fear of what U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan might say in congressional testimony. The All Ordinaries index closed up 6.1 points at 2,391.00.

JOHANNESBURG - South African gold shares ended stronger on a recovery in the bullion price and industrials were soft amid a lack of interest ahead of closed markets for a Human Rights Day holiday on Friday. The All-share index was down 0.9 points to 7,098.6, the Gold index gained 6.6 points to 1,832.2 and the Industrial index shed 20.0 points to 8,322.6.
